analysis:
Modi said at Make in India Week in Mumbai on 13 February 2016 that the government wanted manufacturing's share of GDP to rise to 25% 'in the near future'. The figure comes from the National Manufacturing Policy (2011), which targeted 25% by 2022 and 100 million additional jobs; secondary sources describe the 2022 date as part of Make in India's objectives and later restated as 2025. The 2022 deadline is the policy's, not a date in Modi's quoted sentence.

The measured share has not risen. World Bank data give 15.1% for 2014-15 and 13.1-13.5% in 2024-26. MoSPI-based figures (constant-price GVA share) are higher, about 17.2-18.5%, but also show no sustained increase (17.3% in 2013-14, 17.3% in 2023-24). Both bases fall well short of 25%.

The government has restated the 25% objective with later dates (2025, 2030 or 2047 in various statements).
